target_users.interface: domain, mailbox, alias, retention, migration admin APIs

acceptance_criteria.given: a work mailbox receives a message
acceptance_criteria.then: it is encrypted under tenant DEK, tagged Org pillar, indexed without plaintext, and covered by retention policy

acceptance_criteria.given: a personal mailbox receives a message
acceptance_criteria.then: it is Person pillar and unavailable to org-admin search/export APIs

acceptance_criteria.given: a compliance officer opens a scoped legal hold
acceptance_criteria.then: deletion and retention expiry are blocked until release and all actions are audit chained
source hashes, folder labels, message IDs, and retention class survive import

acceptance_criteria.given: a user turns a work mail into a Workflow item
acceptance_criteria.then: WorkflowHandoffAuditLog links original message, extracted payload, consent/policy basis, and workflow item id

acceptance_criteria.given: an inbound SMTP message arrives for a work domain
acceptance_criteria.when: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC checks complete
acceptance_criteria.then: authentication result is stamped on MailMessage.perimeter_auth_result; messages failing DMARC policy are quarantined or rejected per tenant policy and the action is logged

acceptance_criteria.given: a user composes a new work mail
acceptance_criteria.when: they request AI-assisted compose or thread summarization
acceptance_criteria.then: the assistant operates within the tenant DEK boundary and the composed draft is not transmitted to any model training pipeline; user opt-in is required per tenant policy

acceptance_criteria.given: an outbound mail contains tracking pixels or invisible trackers
acceptance_criteria.when: the MIME pipeline processes the outbound message
acceptance_criteria.then: tracker injection is detected and blocked; a policy event is emitted

acceptance_criteria.given: a user enables confidential mail for a work message
acceptance_criteria.then: the message carries an expiry timestamp and a recipient-access policy; expiry is enforced server-side under legal-hold rules

acceptance_criteria.given: a personal-context mailbox user enables Hide-My-Email aliases
acceptance_criteria.when: they generate an alias for an external service
acceptance_criteria.then: the alias is provisioned in the Person pillar and forwards to the personal mailbox without exposing the real address; alias cannot be queried by org admin

personal_professional_separation.invariant: Mail keeps personal-life and professional-life data in separate tenant/RBAC scopes. Org administrators, legal hold, retention, DLP, search, export, notification routing, bridges, and workflow automation for a professional tenant cannot read, infer, mutate, or route personal context data; personal context actions likewise cannot write into a professional tenant without explicit policy-authorized user action and audit evidence.

tenancy_model.personal_scope: __personal__/<user_id> tenant scope with user-owned keys and personal RBAC subject
tenancy_model.professional_scope: <organization>/<workspace> tenant scope with tenant admin RBAC, retention, legal hold, and audit-chain policy
tenancy_model.shared_infrastructure_rule: shared clusters are permitted only when namespace, service account, network policy, secret, key, storage, search-index, and audit-log boundaries preserve tenant isolation

forbidden_cross_context_flows: professional legal hold or eDiscovery over personal data
personal labels, folders, DMs, or notifications leaking professional content
workflow bridges that copy personal content into professional tenant scope without consent and audit evidence
machine-learning or ranking features training across personal/professional scopes without a policy-specific opt-in and data-use record
